title: Flat locally finitely presented representable maps descend fppf
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $g:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ be morphisms representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Assume $g$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. If the projection $f_{\mathcal C}:\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, then $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Flatness and local finite presentation of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts, using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Surjectivity means that every field-valued object of the target lifts up to isomorphism after a field extension [def-weil-field]. No quasi-compactness or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tags 06PZ (lemma-descent-flat) and 06Q8 (lemma-descent-finite-presentation), each restricted to representable morphisms.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary scheme $T$ and an object $b$ of $\mathcal B$ over $T$, i.e. a map $T\to\mathcal B$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Representability of $f$ and $g$ gives algebraic spaces $X=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}T$ and $Y=\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal B}T$; an object of $Y$ over a $T$-scheme $W$ is a pair $(c,\psi)$ with $c\in\mathcal C(W)$ and $\psi:g(c)\simeq b|_W$, and similarly for $X$. By base-change stability of flatness, local finite presentation and surjectivity in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to $g$ along $T\to\mathcal B$, the projection $q:Y\to T$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. It is representable by algebraic spaces: for a scheme $T^{\prime}\to T$, the functor $(c,\psi)\mapsto(c,\psi)$ identifies $Y\times_TT^{\prime}$ with $\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal B}T^{\prime}$ (for $T^{\prime}\to T\to\mathcal B$), compatibly with arrows and restrictions, and the latter is an algebraic space because $g$ is representable.

source.place: Tags 06PZ (lemma-descent-flat) and 06Q8 (lemma-descent-finite-presentation), proof, first paragraph: reduction of the cover to an algebraic space; here by scheme base change of g

proof.text: Let $P$ be flatness or local finite presentation; the two cases are separate. Write $X_Y=X\times_TY$. On a test scheme $W$ an object of $X_Y$ is $(a,\phi,c,\psi)$ with $\phi:f(a)\simeq b|_W$ and $\psi:g(c)\simeq b|_W$ over one map $W\to T$. An object of $(\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal C)\times_{\mathcal C}Y$ is $((a,c^{\prime},\chi),(c,\psi),\epsilon)$ with $\chi:f(a)\simeq g(c^{\prime})$ and $\epsilon:c^{\prime}\simeq c$. Send it to $(a,\psi\circ g(\epsilon)\circ\chi,c,\psi)$; in the other direction send $(a,\phi,c,\psi)$ to $((a,c,\psi^{-1}\phi),(c,\psi),\mathrm{id})$. The composite in $X_Y$ is the identity, the other composite is isomorphic to the identity via $(\mathrm{id}_a,\epsilon)$, and both functors act on arrows componentwise and commute with restriction by the definition of 2-fibre products [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. So $X_Y\to Y$ is, over $Y$, the pullback of $f_{\mathcal C}$ along $Y\to\mathcal C$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ and a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to X_Y\times_YV$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By the same identification, $X_Y\times_YV\to V$ is the scheme base change of $f_{\mathcal C}$ along $V\to Y\to\mathcal C$, so by the hypothesis on $f_{\mathcal C}$ and the scheme-test meaning of $P$ for representable maps, the scheme map $U\to V$ has $P$. Now [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], with target chart $V\to Y$ and source chart $U$, gives $P(X_Y\to Y)$.

source.place: Tags 06PZ and 06Q8, proof: the base change of the given projection along the new cover is again flat (lemma-base-change-flat), with 2-fibre-product associativity written out

proof.text: Regard $T$ as an algebraic space by its representable sheaf [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. By Step 1, $q:Y\to T$ is a representable surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism from an algebraic space, and by Step 2 the base change $X\times_TY\to Y$ of the morphism of algebraic spaces $X\to T$ has $P$. The assertion for morphisms of algebraic spaces in [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] (each property separately, target-local along such a cover) gives $P(X\to T)$. Since $T\to\mathcal B$ was an arbitrary scheme test, $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by the scheme-test meaning of these properties for representable morphisms. No quasi-compactness of $g$ or $Y\to T$ is used, and the empty cases ($T$ or $Y$ empty) are covered by the cited statement.
